subject: Model selection with indicator variables in a multi-species model

messages.author: 5cedd6d295e20d48
messages.subject: Model selection with indicator variables in a multi-species model
parts:
Hi all,

I have a fairly brief question (let me know if I should provide code). I have a multispecies Bayesian occupancy model, and am using the indicator variable method of model selection/ model averaging from Kery & Royle's AHM book.

We're not sure how to deal with the multi-species part though - I'd expect each species to support a different model, and so would model averaging need to be species-by-species? Or can one simply insert indicator variables as in a single-species model?

Best wishes,
Alexandra

messages.author: 3fac8f4565858af2
messages.subject: Re: Model selection with indicator variables in a multi-species model
parts:
Hi Alexandra,

This is a good question, and I was wondering if you had resolved it since it’s been a few months. I’ve been playing around with the same thing, and so if I understand your question, you are asking if the indicator variable should vary by species or not? In other words, for each model iteration, should the same parameter be included across all species or should it be allowed to vary by species?

I tried it both ways – note that in both cases I sampled a high number of iterations to adequately sample all potential submodels. However, keeping parameter inclusion the same across species for each model iteration caused some convergence issues. I’m not quite sure yet if this is because it over-constrained the model, or if it has something to do with the MCMC sampler having difficulty when the inclusion variable is 0. If it is set to 0 across all species for a single iteration, then this may be too vague for the MCMC sampler to search parameter space.

The model performed better when I allowed inclusion to vary by species. This could be because the heterogeneity of the inclusion variable (1’s allowed whenever 0’s included across species or parameters) served as a check to help the MCMC sampler converge. This could also be because it allowed for more flexibility, and the community I am analyzing is relatively heterogenous – in other words, the species partition habitats such that species-specific effects differ in their strength, across species (i.e., only a few don’t overlap 0, and which one(s) varies by species). 

So, I’m still in the early stages of testing all this, but those are my observations to date, and I welcome any feedback.

Thanks,
Holly

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: Model selection with indicator variables in a multi-species model
parts:
dear all,
 this is a complex issue. I don't agree with having indicator variables that vary by species in this model because the prior distributions are "community level" priors and the variable selection bit is effectively zero-inflating those. That is a weird model for a population (zero inflated normal...). It's not completely inviable but I think some argument needs to be made that this is sensible.  In effect, there is a conflict between what the community prior is doing and what the indicator variables are doing... they are both doing variable selection in a sense. Do you need both? I would avoid it, personally.
regards
andy
